note_summary:
67-year-old male with history of CKD stage 3 and hypertension presented with fever (T 38.4°C), tachycardia (HR 118), and altered mental status. Blood cultures positive for E. coli, consistent with urosepsis. Acute kidney injury on chronic kidney disease — creatinine rose from baseline 1.4 to 3.8 mg/dL. WBC 18.4 K/uL with left shift.

Started on broad-spectrum antibiotics (ceftriaxone 2g IV daily) and aggressive fluid resuscitation. Vasopressor support (norepinephrine) initiated for MAP < 65 mmHg. Trending: heart rate rising over the last 12 hours and MAP declining despite vasopressor support — concerning for septic shock progression. Recommend ICU transfer, source control evaluation, and lactate monitoring.

alerts.message: High mortality risk (42%). Immediate clinical review and ICU consideration recommended.
Creatinine 3.8 mg/dL — severe AKI (KDIGO stage 2-3) on chronic kidney disease. Consider nephrology consult and renal replacement therapy planning.
MAP 62 mmHg — below target (≥65) despite vasopressor support. Evidence of septic shock progression.
Potassium 5.8 mmol/L — hyperkalemia. Continuous ECG monitoring; consider treatment (insulin/dextrose, calcium gluconate).
Heart rate trending upward (slope 1.8 bpm/hr, R²=0.84). Possible compensatory tachycardia for declining MAP.
